Antigo Testamento;Juízes;8;1;1. They Did Chide;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"1. They did chide. Ephraim was the most populous and most important tribe of northern Palestine and was jealous of its position of leadership. The Ephraimites had rallied immediately to Gideon’s call

Repentance involves a change in the basic attitude of the sinner toward his sin. Men generally sin because they love to. Antigo Testamento;1 Reis;8;1;1. Solomon Assembled;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"1. Solomon assembled. The account of the rites connected with the dedication of the Temple constitutes one of the outstanding chapters of the Bible. The narrative is one of great beauty and deep spiritual significance. In it leaders of the church have found words of inspiration and encouragement throughout the centuries for the consecration of houses of worship. This chapter stands in remarkable contrast with the preceding one. There we find the formal and technical details having to do with the material things of the Temple. Here we enter into the deeper significance of the things having to do with the house of God—we come into contact with God Himself. Both chapters have their part in giving us a true and complete picture of the Temple and its significance
column2: and neither would be complete without the other.

column1: Solomon is the important personage leading out in the various activities connected with the dedication of the Temple. His kingly majesty is conspicuous. But he seems to be more than a mere king
column2: engaged only in the secular affairs of state. He is engaged now in a distinctly religious service for God. Such a service would not at all serve to lessen his royal dignity but to enhance it. He performs the functions that as king we would expect of him
column3: and more. He calls together the leaders of the nation and directs in the arrangements made. But having done that
column4: it might be expected that the priests would take over and lead out in the distinctly religious functions. But that is not the case. It is the king who consecrates the sanctuary
column5: who offers the dedicatory prayer

column7: and who pronounces upon them the divine blessing.

column3: selfish disposition of the king

column5: refused to eat

Does a man who is lord of the realm need to admit that he cannot secure a small parcel of ground? Is Ahab the king allowing himself to be thwarted by some insignificant subject of his? The item could be easily handled—she would take care of the matter herself and show him how such things are done.
Antigo Testamento;1 Reis;21;8;8. Letters;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"8. Letters. To Ahab it evidently was a matter of no consequence as to how Jezebel secured the vineyard

column1: Antigo Testamento;1 Reis;21;9;9. A Fast;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"9. A fast. This may have been to cover up the foul crime with a cloak of religious sanctity

column3: if not atoned for

column1: Set Naboth. Not to be honored
column2: but to be tried."

column2: in harmony with judicial requirements (Num. 35:30; Deut. 17:6).

column3: and wickedness—vile scoundrels of whom anything evil could be expected (see Judges 19:22; 20:13; 1 Sam. 1:16; 2:12; 10:27; 25:17

The ready acquiescence of the rulers of the city in carrying out this foul plot is characteristic of the worst to be found in Oriental despotism. The word of the king was law. Even base murder would be carried out under the pretense of justice. This ready submission of the elders and nobles implied a deep moral degradation among the people.

Antigo Testamento;1 Reis;21;13;13. Stoned Him;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"13. Stoned him. It appears from 2 Kings 9:26 that not only Naboth but also his sons were stoned. When Achan was put to death his sons and daughters were stoned with him (Joshua 7:24

Elijah was sent by God to deliver Heaven’s massage. When the Lord has a work to do He finds those who are willing to go on errands for Him."

column1: Antigo Testamento;1 Reis;21;18;18. Samaria;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"18. Samaria. Not the city but the district of Samaria
column2: as in ch. 13:32."

column1: Antigo Testamento;1 Reis;21;19;19. Hast Thou Killed;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"19. Hast thou killed? In Elija’s meeting with Ahab there are to be no polite preliminaries. The prophet comes right to the point

column3: and the king stands forth for what he really is
column4: a shameless marauder and murderer
column5: who slays without pity and then moves in on his victim’s goods.

column2: that shall he also reap” (Gal. 6:7)."

column3: though condemnatory

column1: Tare forty and two. The judgment that followed came from God. The severity of the punishment was in keeping with the seriousness of the issues at stake. I will go. When Jehoshaphat had consented to go with Ahab against the Syrians he was rebuked by the prophet Jehu for giving help to “the ungodly” and loving “them that hate the Lord” (2 Chron. 19:2). But now he again gave his consent to a similar request

column6: Jehoshaphat joined with Ahaziah in an enterprise involving the building of ships at Ezion-geber to engage in foreign trade (2 Chron. 20:35–37). Later Joram had the assistance of Jehoshaphat’s grandson Ahaziah in another war against Syria (2 Chron. 22:5)."

column1: The custom of “pouring water on the hands” of someone as a sign of ministration is still prevalent in the Near East today. Water is scarce in most Bible lands

Then a thin stream of water is poured over their hands from a spouted jug or a metal vessel that resembles a teapot. column4: and not the man of honor."

Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;1;1. Of the Wives;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"1. Of the wives. This is an important revelation concerning the nature of the “sons of the prophets.” They were not young
column2: unmarried men
column3: living lives of seclusion in monastic establishments; they were men of the people. They were of the people
column4: lived with the people
column5: and labored for the people. Instead of being interested only in themselves
column6: living together in ascetic communities and seeking there to attain unto holiness
column7: they lived for the good of the nation
column8: seeking not their own material gain but the common good of all about them.

column1: Fear the Lord. This man was a faithful worshiper of Jehovah. The influence of Elijah and Elisha had done much to promote the worship of the true God throughout the kingdom of Israel.
The creditor is come. The law of Moses recognized servitude for debt
column2: not as a “bondservant” but “as an hired servant
column3: and as a sojourner
column4: ” and required that the individual thus sold serve only till the year of jubilee (Lev. 25:39–42). In the present instance it would seem that the creditor had not enforced his right over the sons during the lifetime of the debtor
column5: but on his death made claim upon their services
column6: that the obligation of the father might be fulfilled."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;2;2. What Shall I Do;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"2. What shall I do? The question revealed the kindly spirit of the prophet. Elisha was a man who was interested in the people
column2: always friendly
column3: always sympathetic
column4: and always ready to help. When called upon by the king
column5: he was ready to supply the wants of the whole army
column6: when called on by a poor and friendless widow
column7: he did not turn her away.

column1: What hast thou? God uses what we have. He is not limited in His resources or His powers
column2: and could easily have supplied the woman’s need without her pot of oil. But He took what she had and placed His blessing upon it. So it is with God’s servants today. They may not have much in natural ability or material resources
column3: but if they devote what they have to God and His service
column4: asking for His blessing
column5: the little they have is increased manyfold. Man in his efforts to help the poor would do well to think in terms of helping them to help themselves. The poor should be taught to employ such resources as they themselves possess. Unless this is done
column6: charity may pauperize and do more harm than good.

column1: Save a pot of oil. The pot of oil was not much
column2: but in God’s hand and with His blessing it was sufficient to supply all her needs. Our talents may not be many and our measure of worldly wealth may not be large
column3: but God can use and increase whatever is devoted to Him. The pot of oil was the sign of the widow’s utmost poverty
column4: but it was also the means employed by the Lord for the supplying of all her needs."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;3;3. Borrow Not a Few;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"3. Borrow not a few. The widow’s response would be the measure of her faith
column2: and also the measure of what she was to receive from the Lord. With little faith she would have received little
column3: with large faith she would receive much."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;5;5. She Poured Out;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"5. She poured out. The widow did not stumble because of unbelief. She responded immediately to the prophet’s instructions
column2: and enlisted also the cooperation of her sons. If the sons were to be saved from lives of servitude
column3: they also had something to do for themselves. Her faith and obedience engendered faith and obedience in her sons. Faith gives rise to faith
column4: and obedience on the part of one encourages obedience on the part of others."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;6;6. The Oil Stayed;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"6. The oil stayed. God can no longer give when man is no longer prepared to receive. Not until the last vessel had been filled
column2: did the miraculous supply of oil cease to flow."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;7;7. Pay Thy Debt;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"7. Pay thy debt. The widow received more from the Lord than she had asked for. Her request was only that her sons be delivered from lives of servitude. But in her poverty
column2: she still had many needs. God undertook to supply those needs. He constantly gives to men blessings far greater than they ask for themselves."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;8;8. Shunem;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"8. Shunem. A town in the Valley of Jezreel
column2: about 5 mi. (8 km.) north-northwest of Mt. Gilboa
column3: and perhaps 16 mi. (25.6 km.) or more from Mt. Carmel
column4: where Elisha at this time seems to have made his home (v. 25). In his journeys to and fro through the kingdom
column5: Elisha frequently passed through this village
column6: now Sôlem.

column1: A great woman. That is
column2: a rich woman (see 1 Sam. 25:2; 2 Sam. 19:32)
column3: or one of high rank.

column1: Constrained him. To Elisha was extended the hospitality of this comfortable home. Men of God have the same needs of food and shelter as their fellows
column2: and they appreciate the blessings of Christian fellowship and friendship. Life for a faithful servant of God is often made happy and pleasant by kindly courtesies extended to him by those whom he is here to serve."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;10;10. A Little Chamber;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"10. A little chamber. Riches often make the possessor self-centered and forgetful of the needs and desires of others. But this was evidently not the case with this noble woman of Shunem. She was a great woman
column2: but she did not lose the common touch. She lived not for herself alone but strove to make others happy. Having her own needs well provided for
column3: she shared her possessions with others. She had her own household cares and responsibilities
column4: but she did not allow the duties of her home to make her forgetful of the needs and comforts of Elisha and perhaps many others. On his journeys Elisha often looked forward to the pleasant hours of rest and relaxation that would be his when he arrived at the village of Shunem. Kindly hospitality helps to bring among the children of earth a little of the peace and friendship of heaven."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;12;12. Call This Shunammite;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;12. Call this Shunammite. The Shunammite had been kind to Elisha and he would be kind to her. But what could he do to repay her for the favors she had bestowed on him? She did not need material things. But Elisha wanted to give her some token of his appreciation. A noble heart does not like to receive a favor and make no return.
Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;13;13. What is to Be Done;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"13. What is to be done? The question was a test question
column2: for it would reveal exactly what was in the woman’s heart. Had she received the prophet in the name of a prophet
column3: or did she have a secret desire for some reward?

column1: Spoken for to the king. Elisha recognized the fact that he had some influence at the court and with the nation’s highest authorities. Might there be some matter in which Elisha could enlist for the woman of Shunem the assistance of the king?
Among mine own people. The answer conveys the idea that she was perfectly contented. She was living at peace with her own people and had no quarrels with neighbors
column2: nor any matters that could not be settled with her friends. It was a peaceful and happy community
column3: and neither the king nor his servants could do anything to make life the happier."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;14;14. What Then is to Be Done;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"14. What then is to be done? To do something for a person who already was perfectly happy and who had all she needed of this world’s goods was not easy
column2: but Elisha persisted in his endeavor to discover something in which he might be of service to her.

column1: She hath no child. Regarded by every Hebrew woman as a distinct misfortune and a reproach (see Gen. 30:23; Deut. 7:13
Her husband is old. Much as she might desire a child
column2: she believed there was no longer any hope
column3: for her husband was old."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;15;15. In the Door;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"15. In the door. Perhaps from modesty and good manners
column2: for it might not have been proper for her to have entered into Elisha’s chamber."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;16;16. Thou Shalt Embrace a Son;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"16. Thou shalt embrace a son. What is impossible with men is not impossible with God. If she desired a son
column2: God could make that possible for her. Elisha’s promise to her of a son within the year was far beyond her fondest hopes.

column1: Do not lie. Do not deceive me by setting before me hopes that cannot be realized. Compare the incredulity of Abraham (Gen. 17:17)
column2: of Sarah (Gen. 18:12)
column3: and of Zacharias (Luke 1:20)
column4: when promised a child."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;17;17. At That Season;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"17. At that season. A true prophet of the Lord does not make false predictions in the name of the Lord. As Elisha had promised
column2: so it came to pass."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;19;19. My Head;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"19. My head. Probably a case of sunstroke. Reaping was a strenuous task
column2: carried on at the hottest season of the year."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;20;20. Then Died;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"20. Then died. Sorrow and joy
column2: tears and laughter
column3: life and death
column4: are not far apart in the sojourn of mortal man in this world of sin. The son of the Shunammite had brought gladness into the home
column5: but he was also the means of bringing anguish of heart. He had been given to the Shunammite by the Lord
column6: but now death claimed him as it own."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;22;22. Send Me;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"22. Send me. It was the busy harvest season
column2: and all the men and animals of this large establishment were in the field. But she asked for the immediate use of one of the animals and its driver.

column1: To the man of God. As a dutiful wife
column2: the woman informed her husband of the journey she proposed to make and of the fact that she planned on an early return
column3: but she did not explain the reason for her trip. Perhaps if she had informed him of her intention to call the prophet to raise her son
column4: who was already dead
column5: he might have deemed the journey useless and might have made an endeavor to dissuade her from her purpose. The matter was one of faith
column6: and she seemed to keep it strictly between herself and God."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;23;"23. Neither New Moon
column2: Nor Sabbath";Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"23. Neither new moon
column3: nor sabbath. Both were holy days
column4: occasions for offerings and solemn assemblies (2 Chron. 2:4; Isa. 1:13; Hosea 2:11; Amos 8:5). Evidently on such days it must have been customary for the people to assemble for purposes of worship or religious instruction and edification. If it had been either the new moon or the Sabbath

column6: but as it was
column7: the husband could not understand her purpose.

column1: It shall be well. Literally
column2: “peace.” The answer was one of faith and of hope. The child was dead
column3: but she did not give way to grief or despair. If the man of God could intercede with God to provide the child in the first place
column4: he could also have power with God to restore the child. However difficult a matter may be
column5: when we commit a thing into the hands of God
column6: we may have perfect assurance that it will be well. The answer may not always be exactly what we desire
column7: but we can have peace
column8: and bow humbly and submissively to His will."

column3: but she had only one thought
column4: and that was to reach Elisha at the earliest possible moment."

column2: whence it commanded a view of a large part of the valley below. Elisha saw the woman in the distance and recognized her."

column2: and without waiting for her to approach him
column3: sent his servant to meet her
column4: to ascertain if possible the reason for her coming.

column1: It is well. Again her answer was
column2: literally
column3: “Peace.” The burden of her heart would be revealed only to the prophet
column4: not to his servant."

To thrust her away. The unfeeling servant failed to grasp the situation
column2: and endeavored roughly to brush her aside.

column1: Her soul is vexed. Elisha saw at once that some uncontrollable grief had filled the woman’s soul
column2: and his heart went out to her in tender sympathy. The true child of God whose heart is filled with love and sympathy will be moved with compassion toward all who are heavy laden
column3: and
column4: like his Master
column5: he will endeavor to give them rest. True love is tender and kind
column6: and responds to the appeal of those who find themselves in need.

column1: Hid it from me. At times the Lord saw fit to reveal to His servant the circumstances of a particular person
column2: but not always. No prophet is in possession of all knowledge. Revelations are made only in accordance with God’s will. The fact that a prophet does not know all the facts connected with a particular matter is no evidence that he is not a true prophet of the Lord. Prophets also are men
column3: and their knowledge and judgment
column4: like that of other men
column5: are limited. Only when God gives to them special revelations and wisdom do their words posses unique authority. The idea that in such instances as this a prophet should be in possession of all the facts is unwarranted."

column2: now has been taken from her. She does not say this in so many words; she does not need to
column3: for Elisha now understands fully the meaning of her grief. Her words reveal the bitterness of her sorrow. She knows only that this son
column4: whom she did not demand
column5: is gone and that her grief is infinitely greater than if she had never been permitted to know his love."

column2: and that the way back would be all the more difficult and trying. He did not shun the journey himself
column3: but as soon as he knew that the child was dead
column4: he dispatched his servant with instructions as to his course of action.

column2: and like Moses’ rod (Ex. 4:17; Ex. 17:5
column5: was the symbol of the power of God wherewith he would perform miracles in the name of the Lord.

column2: but that he was to lose no time on the way. Salutations in the East are long and ceremonious
column3: and politeness takes time."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;30;30. I Will Not Leave Thee;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"30. I will not leave thee. The woman had more faith in Elisha than in his servant. She knew the power of Elisha’s prayers and ministry

column3: there is power in the gospel to heal and restore. All the evil that sin has wrought the Holy Spirit has power to undo. God has the antidote to every form of evil. Christ is the source of life eternal for every man who has the will to live (John 6:27

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;4;0;Ellen G. White Comments;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"ELLEN G. WHITE COMMENTS
Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;5;1;1. Naaman;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"1. Naaman. Syria was often at war with Israel
column2: but this was evidently a period of peace. Only a short time before
column3: Ahab had been slain in battle against Benhadad (1 Kings 22:34–37). The name of the king of Israel is not given

column3: he retained his position as commander of the Syrian hosts
column4: although he must have been seriously handicapped by the terrible disease with which he was afflicted."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;5;2;2. By Companies;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"2. By companies. There were frequent border raids conducted by marauding bands
column2: usually carried on for purposes of plunder.

column1: Waited on Naaman’s wife. The captive maid was living the life of a slave

column3: her heart went out in sympathy to her ailing master and his wife. Instead of wishing Naaman ill because of the misfortunes that had been brought upon her

column6: she believed He could also perform toward those of an alien race.

column1: One went in. That is
column2: Naaman went to his lord the king of Syria and related to him the words of the captive maid. Little did the girl understand the import of her words of faith in God. Naaman believed because the girl believed

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;5;5;5. I Will Send;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"5. I will send. Not only had the young maiden’s testimony of faith created confidence in the commander of the Syrian hosts

column4: and in offering his services to Naaman

column3: the Lord who gave life and hope to man. If every child of God were as faithful in bearing witness for Him as the captive Hebrew maid

column5: and many would be led to give praise and thanksgiving to Him."

column3: which was devoted to the worship of idols

column7: and in his treatment of Naaman

column9: not with a word of rebuke but with a message of peace similar to that contained in Jesus’ farewell to His disciples (John 14:27)."

column5: and now the commander of the armies of Syria

column3: when the inhabitants of Jerusalem found themselves in a similar crisis
column4: Jeremiah was consulted for guidance and information concerning the will of the Lord (Jer. 21:1

column4: the son of a murderer

column6: the upright
column7: law-abiding citizen. Murder is as wrong for a king as for any ordinary individual within the realm.

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;6;0;Ellen G. White Comments;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"ELLEN G. WHITE COMMENTS
Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;1;1. The Word of the Lord;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"1. The word of the Lord. The king of Israel had expressed his opinion

column4: and having turned against the Lord

column6: in the hope of finding some means of relief. Elisha reveals that it is God and not the king who will provide relief.

column1: Measure. Heb. se’ah. Six cabs were equal to a seah

column3: p. 167). On one day “the fourth part of a cab of dove’s dung” sold for “five pieces of silver” (ch. 6:25). But on the next day 24 times that amount of wheat would be sold for a fifth the price. Or in other words
column4: the amount of money that during the famine would purchase a bit of the cheapest and lowliest product that could be used to sustain life
column5: would on the following day purchase 120 times as much of the best wheat flour.

column1: The gate of Samaria. In Oriental cities where access is had to cities by gates through the city walls

column3: one of the gates of Samaria would be the center of distribution."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;2;2. A Lord;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"2. A lord. Heb. hashshalish
column2: literally

column4: ” or “the thirdling.” Originally

column6: as among the Hittites. The Assyrians assigned only two men to each of their chariots. Later it became the title of an important functionary in Oriental courts. When Jehu slew Joram

column8: Bidkar

column13: where food would be offered for sale (ch. 7:16–18). The fact that this officer was present at this time at the home of Elisha suggests that the king was likewise present (see on ch. 6:33).

column2: but because of his unbelief he would not be permitted to participate in the blessings it would bring."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;3;3. At the Entering in;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"3. At the entering in. Being lepers

column3: 3). They were thus without the city walls
column4: but near the gate.

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;5;5. In the Twilight;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"5. In the twilight. They waited till nightfall

column3: who might consider their scheme an act of desertion.

column1: The uttermost part. That is

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;6;6. To Hear a Noise;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"6. To hear a noise. For similar examples
column2: see on ch. 6:19.

column3: the force of any national group could at some time or other find itself arrayed against almost any other people.

column2: and their forces could provide a serious threat to the armies of Syria.

This was the time of the Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt (see on 1 Kings 14:25) when the capital was at Bubastis in the eastern Delta and Egypt was ruled by a dynasty of Lybian kings. The “kings of the Egyptians” undoubtedly refers to certain minor and subsidiary kinglets rather than to the king of Egypt proper."

Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;7;7. They Arose and Fled;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"7. They arose and fled. The picture is one of wild and precipitous flight. Believing themselves surrounded by enemies on every side

column3: each man thinking only of his own safety. Everything was left behind."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;8;8. Did Eat;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;8. Did eat. The lepers thought first of satisfying their gnawing hunger. Then they responded to the natural impulse of helping themselves to the treasure that was simply waiting to be carried away.
Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;9;9. We Do Not Well;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"9. We do not well. They were not doing well
column2: but they were a long time finding it out. Inside the city
column3: men
column4: women
column5: and children were starving
column6: but all this time the lepers were interested only in themselves. By allowing their countrymen to perish within reach of plenty

Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;11;11. The Porters;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;11. The porters. The warders or keepers of the gate.

Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;12;12. I Will Now Shew You;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"12. I will now shew you. column2: “two horse chariots.” According to the LXX the men went on horseback."

column3: but the Hebrew messengers were determined to ascertain the facts. Everything indicated that the Syrians had fled in abject terror
column4: discarding anything that might hinder their flight."

Under every circumstances it pays to ascertain the word of the Lord. That word is always true. What God says will surely come to pass. He who has faith in God may walk a path that is altogether sure. column2: he might have given his people a message of hope. If he had accepted the words of Elisha
column3: he might have rested in peace and set before his people an example of courage and trust. Man always loses when he refuses to believe the word of the Lord. Faith in God is the way of wisdom and life. It brings to man joy and peace in this world

At the news of the Syrians’ flight there would be only one thought in the minds of all—to get out of the city gate and find food. The situation was not easy to control. In all probability the king at this vital hour also chose to take his position at the city gate
column2: perhaps above it
column3: on the city wall
column4: where he would have a good view both of the city and the Syrian camp."

column3: immorality
column4: intemperance
column5: and cruelty were to be seen on every hand. Temples of worship became seats of iniquity. God’s chosen people had strayed far from righteousness and the ways of holiness and peace. They needed to learn anew concerning God

column7: that He loved His people

column9: justice
column10: and truth. Under Israel’s present circumstances these lessons were exceedingly hard to learn. Ordinary measures did not suffice. Therefore such men as Elijah and Elisha were sent
column11: proclaiming messages of rebuke and appeal and working singular miracles. The result was that many were brought back again to reason and righteousness and to faith and obedience to God. Holy men of God were living out before their fellows the life and love of God
column12: and as a consequence a new spirit and hope were coming back into the hearts and lives of men. Once more the peace and righteousness of heaven were beginning to be seen among the children of earth. The work of Elisha was not in vain."

column1: Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;7;0;Ellen G. White Comments;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"ELLEN G. WHITE COMMENTS
Antigo Testamento;2 Reis;8;1;1. Then;Comentário Bíblico Adventista II;"1. Then. Heb. we

column3: under similar conditions
column4: had gone down to Egypt to sojourn there (Gen. 12:10). Naomi had sojourned in the land of Moab “about ten years” (Ruth 1:4). So now

column1: All the great things. The life stories of Elijah and Elisha are full of many interesting incidents and have a touching and dramatic appeal. column2: in the land of Israel and in countries abroad. Reduced to writing
column3: they were collected and brought into the sacred record of the Hebrews
column4: for our encouragement and enlightenment in this modern age. What God did then He is able and willing to do again today. No stories ever fall upon mortal ears with greater interest and more soul-stirring power than those that tell how God works through His human agents His mighty wonders to perform."
